subject: Re: Vantage platform migration — commercial bridge & concession options
messages:
From: Jordan Ames <j.ames@vantage.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria@vantage.ai>; procurement@vantage.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vantage pricing ask + migration incentives

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the product overview last week — the performance numbers look promising. We are finalizing our economics for a potential Q3 migration and I wanted to be transparent about where we are coming from: our incumbent is offering a blended TCO with an up-front credit and a 9-month ramp that effectively reduces our first-year spend by ~32%.

Before we proceed with a technical pilot, procurement and finance want to understand whether Redwood can (a) match the net economic outcome (credits + rebates) or (b) provide a structured migration bridge that preserves our unit economics while we ramp usage. If you can put together a concrete concession structure and a short plan for the migration timeline, we can fast-track approvals — we have internal deadlines the week of Mar 29.

A few asks to help us compare apples-to-apples:
- Example pricing with the same volume profile (attached sample CSV)
- Any pilot credits or onboarding assistance available
- Typical ramp/seat credits you grant (structure + cap)
- Contract term and early-exit handling in a migration scenario

Can you respond by EOD Mar 17? Appreciate it.

— Jordan
Procurement, Vantage AI

(attachment: vantage_volume_sample.csv (csv))

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ames <j.ames@vantage.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vantage pricing ask + migration incentives

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the sample volumes. I put together an initial commercial bridge and a side-by-side econ compare (see attached v1). High-level summary up front: we can close the gap you described with a combination of a pilot credit, a time-limited ramp credit, and a small onboarding professional services discount — all conditioned on a 12-month committed term.

Quick bullets:
- Pilot: $75k credit against first-month usage for a 30-day technical pilot (applies only to usage during pilot).
- Migration bridge: 6 months of ramp credits that step down: 50% credit month 1, 35% month 2–3, 15% month 4–6. Cap at $350k total.
- Onboarding PS: 20% discount on professional services hours (capped).
- Contract: 12-month term, 30-day notice for non-renewal, migration escape hatch with prorated credits if we miss SLOs in first 90 days (need legal to sign off).

Attached: vantage_pricing_comparison_v1.xlsx (side-by-side, modeled to your sample profile) and mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (timeline + milestones).

Next step: I'll need approvals from Sales Ops and Finance for the total concession cap. Looping in Lauren and Marcus to accelerate. Happy to jump on a call this week to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(attachment: vantage_pricing_comparison_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet); mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (doc))

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vantage pricing ask + migration incentives — need finance input

Team — quick review of Nikhil's proposal attached. Two notes: 1) the $350k cap is within reason for a strategic account if we believe the ARR profile holds; 2) we should spell out the conditions that trigger the ramp credits (e.g., signed MSA + monthly usage reporting + migration milestones met).

Marcus — can you confirm whether the concession table is approvable from a margin and ASC revenue recognition perspective? If not fully approvable, please propose an alternate structure (e.g., spread credits over invoices vs. one-time contractor credits). We need an approved wording to share with Jordan by EOD Monday.

Thanks — Lauren
Director, Sales Operations

(attachment: redwood_concession_summary_20270316.pdf (pdf))

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vantage pricing ask + migration incentives — finance review

Lauren / Nikhil — reviewed the numbers. Finance is comfortable with a capped concession approach provided we: 1) amortize credits evenly over the first 6 invoice periods for revenue recognition, and 2) require a minimum commitment (12-month) and an agreed usage reporting cadence.

Alternative if legal wants simpler language: We can structure the bridge as "prepaid usage credits" invoiced up-front at net-zero (credit issued on invoice) so that recognition is straightforward. Either approach keeps the gross-to-net impact contained.

My recommended final commercial terms to present:
- Pilot credit: $75k (applies as a usage credit on the first invoice after pilot)
- Ramp credit: $300k capped, amortized over first 6 months (or issued as invoiced credit if preferred)
- PS discount: 20% capped at $40k
- Required: signed MSA + MIP (mutual action plan) within 21 days of LOI, monthly usage reporting for first 6 months

Copying Priyom for legal redline readiness. If we get a confirm from Jordan, I can OK the concession and finance will prepare the memo for accounting.

— Marcus
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ames <j.ames@vantage.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria@vantage.ai>; Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>; Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>; Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>; Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Final offer: migration bridge & pilot structure for Vantage (VG-2027-1487)

Jordan — following internal review, here's our consolidated offer (we can run the counterparty LOI/term sheet if you want):

Offer highlights (final):
- Pilot credit: $75,000 credit applied to the first invoice after a 30-day technical pilot (pilot to be completed by June 1).
- Ramp credits: $300,000 total cap applied as usage credits across first 6 months post-go-live (amortized for accounting; invoiced credits available on request). Step-down schedule: 50% month 1, 35% months 2–3, 15% months 4–6.
- PS: 20% discount on onboarding services, up to $40,000.
- Commitment: 12-month term with monthly reporting for first 6 months and the mutual action plan milestones attached.
- SLO escape clause: if Redwood misses agreed latency/uptime SLOs in first 90 days we will issue additional remedial credits (TBD in legal redline).

Attachments: redwood_concession_summary_20270316.pdf; mutual_action_plan_v2.docx; vantage_pricing_comparison_v1.xlsx

Next steps: if this aligns, please confirm by replying to this thread and we will prepare a short LOI and draft MSA for your counsel. If you want tweaks to the step-down schedule vs. cap, we can iterate but the $300k cap is the firm commercial limit from finance.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize details.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
